label: first input token is x (t=0)
explanation: Fires only at step 0 when the first original token is the letter x, at a constant magnitude (1.99 every time). Nothing modulates magnitude: it does not vary with sequence length L, digit count or repeats. It never fires on x at any later step (original, delimiter or copy phase), and never on any other token at step 0. In effect it is a fixed embedding-like detector for (x, position 0).

issues: None found. The test split matches perfectly: precision, recall, F1, mass recall and correlation are all 1.0 (16528 active steps, 16528 predicted). The misses command on the test split returned 0 missed activations and 0 false positives.

The dev profile backs every factual claim. Magnitude has mean, median and max all equal to 1.990, so it is constant. All activation mass is at t=0 / orig_idx=0, with zero activations in the delimiter and copy phases and at every t >= 1. The rate falls as L grows only because there are more steps per sequence; activation counts are flat across L=4..9 (about 2700 each), so L does not modulate the feature.
